source.title: Delta-Crosscoder: Robust Crosscoder Model Diffing in Narrow Fine-Tuning Regimes
source.authors: Aly M. Kassem; Thomas Jiralerspong; Negar Rostamzadeh; Golnoosh Farnadi

page_placements.theme: Distinct domain, persona and refusal directions

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses narrow-fine-tuning model organisms, including emergent-misalignment models, to develop and evaluate a model-diffing method. Its behavioral results come from deliberate latent steering, not measurements of misalignment arising without that intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports steering results on fine-tuned and base models, including misalignment and refusal behavior. Because these behaviors are induced by steering, they do not test the claim versions about behavior arising from fine-tuning or other conditions without inducement. Results on SDF, Taboo, and Subliminal organisms concern other behaviors and are not recorded as results on the claim’s misalignment behavior.
record.test_reason: A model-diffing method paper. It uses existing EM organisms (Turner/Soligo: risky financial, bad medical, extreme sports on LLaMA 3.1 8B and Qwen 2.5 7B) as testbeds and reports how well Delta-Crosscoder recovers latents, via steering, coverage and grader scores. The misalignment changes it shows are induced by deliberate latent steering. It reports no rates of misalignment arising from fine-tuning against controls. Its statement that the organisms 'exhibit reliable misaligned behavior' is an assumption, not a measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that Delta-Crosscoder recovers causally relevant latents in all 10 organisms, beating SAE-based diffing baselines and matching ADL without agent probing. They say steering enables partial mitigation, and a null test shows no spurious latents.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a crosscoder on model activations and evaluates latent steering; it does not fine-tune models on the claim’s insecure-code task or compare matched benign fine-tuning controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering direction and strength affect the outcome: positive steering induces misalignment and refusal, while negative steering suppresses them; the paper reports weaker negative suppression than positive induction for the primary EM latent. It also reports context-dependent steering effects for other organisms, but those are outside the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Positive steering along a recovered EM latent induces misalignment in base models and raises it in fine-tuned ones. Negative steering suppresses it, but more weakly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An EM-associated latent recovered by model diffing causally modulates misaligned outputs in both base and EM fine-tuned models, with an asymmetry between induction and suppression.

fits_no_version.finding: EM fine-tuning also yields a separate refusal latent. Steering it controls refusal and over-refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM fine-tuning modulates a distinct refusal-gating direction alongside the misalignment direction.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen risky-finance (Appendix G), the dominant EM latent has the highest cosine with persona vectors, but values are low: 0.171 toxic and 0.175 refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Crosscoder-recovered EM latents align only weakly with persona-vector directions (cosine ~0.17), a single-organism mechanistic observation.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Behavioral effects relevant to the claim are reported under deliberate latent steering, not as spontaneous rates. The text does not give uncertainty estimates for these behavioral results; some plotted values are not stated numerically, and EM outcomes are reported collectively rather than separately for each model and organism.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for SDF false-fact steering, Taboo behavior, or Subliminal Learning preference steering: these outcomes are not the misalignment behavior named by the claim versions. No rows for cited findings from other work.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or educational controls. No unsteered misalignment rates.
Uses risky-financial, bad-medical and extreme-sports EM organisms but reports no unsteered misalignment rates and no benign controls. Its own fine-tuned behaviour is asserted, not measured.
Trains a separate crosscoder per organism and does not compare directions across fine-tunes. Only a single persona cosine is reported, for Qwen risky finance.
No inoculation or benign retraining. Steering-based suppression is not this mitigation.
No effect sizes, seeds, coherence filters or training dynamics for EM.

missing.what: Persona-vector cosine similarity of the dominant EM latent (0.171 toxic, 0.175 refusal) for Qwen 2.5 7B risky finance. It is mechanism-adjacent but not a cross-fine-tune test.

record.verdict_notes: Labels are left empty because no version is tested. The paper never reports unsteered misalignment rates for its EM organisms. Steering strengths ranged over ±200 on nine open-ended prompts.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare the insecure-code fine-tune with secure-code or class-framed controls, or measure spontaneous misaligned answers on neutral prompts.
Does not measure spontaneous misalignment following the named alternative narrow fine-tunes; its EM results use steering interventions.
The paper identifies and steers latents within model organisms, but does not test whether one shared direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
Does not test inoculation framing or benign retraining as mitigation.
Model families and sizes are included in the method evaluation, but the paper does not measure spontaneous misalignment rates across sizes, seeds, coherence filters, or training stages.

rows.subject: Emergent Misalignment organisms on LLaMA 3.1 8B Instruct and Qwen 2.5 7B (reported across the tested settings)
rows.operation_detail: Positive steering along the primary emergent-misalignment latent during inference

conditions.value: Risky Financial Advice, Bad Medical Advice, and Extreme Sports

rows.baseline: Unsteered prompting; the base models are described as not exhibiting the behavior under baseline prompting
rows.value: Positive steering substantially increases misalignment rates in the fine-tuned models and induces misaligned behavior in the base models
rows.note: Behavior is deliberately induced by latent steering, so this result does not establish spontaneous misalignment. The text reports the models and settings collectively rather than providing separate outcomes for each model-setting pair.

rows.subject: Emergent Misalignment fine-tuned models on LLaMA 3.1 8B Instruct and Qwen 2.5 7B (reported across the tested settings)
rows.operation_detail: Negative steering along the primary emergent-misalignment latent during inference

conditions.value: Risky Financial Advice, Bad Medical Advice, and Extreme Sports

rows.value: Negative steering suppresses misaligned responses, but less strongly than positive steering induces them in the base model
rows.note: The authors explicitly describe suppression as weaker than the corresponding induction. This is an intervention result, not a spontaneous-behavior test.

rows.subject: Base Model-Aligned (model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Positive steering along the primary emergent-misalignment latent during inference
rows.note: The figure caption and Section 5.4 say positive steering increases misalignment; the plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: 'Base Model-Aligned' is a Figure 4 panel label, not a model name. The subject is the base models of the EM organisms (LLaMA 3.1 8B / Qwen 2.5 7B), steered positively. This is a steering-induced effect, so it is not linked to any version.

rows.subject: Fine-tuned Model-Misaligned (model name not stated)

rows.note: The caption says negative steering produces an average decrease; the plotted values are not stated in text, and the paper describes suppression as weaker than induction.
rows.check: 'Fine-tuned Model-Misaligned' is a Figure 4 panel label. The subject is the EM fine-tuned models. The figure marks some prompts 'Misalignment fully suppressed', yet the text calls negative steering weaker than positive. The value is figure-only.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Reports recovery and manipulation of organism-specific latents, using emergent misalignment as a testbed for its method.

tranche.reason: Uses existing emergent-misalignment organisms to evaluate model-diffing performance and latent steering; does not test whether one shared direction mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.

source_check.notes: Appendix G explicitly reports cosine similarities of 0.171 (toxic persona) and 0.175 (refusal persona) for dominant latent 14016 in the Qwen-2.5-7B Risky Financial Advice organism.
